challenges.name: page-not-updating-quiz
challenges.title: Why does the course page keep the old price?
challenges.description: The AI-generated caching change and the instructor dashboard's server actions: read what a mismatched tag does, and what the instructor sees after revalidateTag and after updateTag.

questions.explanation: False. A tag is an arbitrary string. Nothing compares the strings passed to cacheTag with the strings passed to updateTag or revalidateTag, and expiring a tag that no entry carries is not an error: it simply expires nothing. Here course:42 and course-42 are different strings, so every save leaves the cached course data in place until cacheLife ends it, up to an hour later. The misconception is that tags are checked like identifiers; to catch a mismatch you need one helper that builds the tag for readers and writers, and a test that saves and then reads.

True. In Next.js 16, revalidateTag(tag, "max") marks the tagged entries stale: the next request is served the old content while a fresh copy is built in the background, and the request after that gets the fresh copy (stale-while-revalidate). That is right for background events, but an instructor who just saved expects to see the change. updateTag, available only in Server Actions, expires the entries at once, so the next request waits for fresh data. The misconception is that every revalidation function removes the entry immediately; check which one you call, and in which version.

challenges.name: spot-the-ai-mistake-course-page-never-updates
challenges.title: Spot the AI Mistake: the course page that never updates
challenges.description: The request sent to an AI coding assistant was: "Cache the course page so it is fast." The assistant cached the course data with getCourse = cached(..., { tags: course:<id>, revalidate: 3600 }) and kept the two server actions of the instructor dashboard, saveCourseDetails and changeCoursePrice. The page is fast and the public tests pass. Since the merge, instructors report that the course page keeps the old title and the old price after they save, for up to an hour, and learners saw 249000 VND on the course page but 199000 VND at checkout. Fix the assistant's code so that after a successful save of a title or a price, the very next read of that course page shows the new value (a MISS that waits for fresh data, not a stale page), while caching keeps working: repeated reads are HITs, other courses stay cached when one course changes, and a rejected action (unknown course, empty title, invalid price) changes nothing and refreshes nothing. The starter contains a model of the Next.js data cache on a fake clock: updateTag(tag) expires entries at once, revalidateTag(tag, "max") marks them stale (the next read still returns the old value), and tags are compared as whole strings. The runner reads { courses, steps } where a step is { read }, { edit, title }, { price, amount } or { advance } (seconds), prints one line per step (a read prints the page and MISS, HIT or STALE) and finally the number of database reads. Do not change the database, the mini cache or the runner.
hints: After saveCourseDetails runs, which cached entry should become out of date, and by what string was that entry labelled when it was stored? Then ask the same question for changeCoursePrice.

Put the tags side by side: the one in the tags option of getCourse and the one each action passes to the cache. Look at every character. Then check the second action: does it tell the cache anything at all? Finally, choose between the two cache functions by what the instructor must see on the next read.

A similar case on a different page: getLesson is cached with tags [`lesson:${id}`], and the action saveLessonBody calls updateTag(`lessons/${id}`). Reading lesson 5, saving its body and reading again prints the old body as a HIT. With one helper lessonTag(id) used by both the reader and the action, the read after the save is a MISS with the new body, and the read after that is a HIT; lesson 6, read before the save, is still a HIT.
